title: [AUG-137] RCA AUG-136: GPU switch missing on Diagnostics screen, v0.0.28 still starts on CPU
why_we_need_this: AUG-136 shipped in v0.0.28 but the user still sees "Transcription runs on CPU" on the Diagnostics screen (SetupGuide.tsx) with all-green checks and no way to switch or install the GPU engine there. Health already reports nvidiaGpu.detected=true (RTX 4060) and gpuEngine=cpu, so the switch exists only in Settings and is not discoverable. A fresh install defaults to CPU with no prompt, so the user's expectation (works on GPU out of the box / switch visible where the CPU message is shown) is not met. Root cause to confirm: AUG-136 acceptance criteria covered Settings and a diagnostics hint, but the hint on the screen the user actually sees has no action.
acceptance_criteria:
1. On the Diagnostics screen (SetupGuide), when nvidiaGpu.detected and gpuEngine is cpu, the "runs on CPU" line is followed by a "Switch to GPU (NVIDIA)" button that calls the same POST /api/engine/switch and shows CUDA download progress (~457 MB) inline, then refreshes health.
2. After the switch completes, Diagnostics shows GPU (CUDA) and transcription actually runs on GPU (verified on this RTX 4060 machine with a real recording; perf-stats gpu=true).
3. Packaged Windows build behaves the same as dev: verify with the installed app that health reports nvidiaGpu detected, the button appears, download completes and engine persists after restart.
4. If WHISPER_GPU_ENGINE env pins the engine, the button is hidden/disabled with a plain-language reason; no backend names or DLL names in UI.
5. macOS and Windows without NVIDIA: Diagnostics unchanged.
6. Brandbook rules respected (0 border-radius, yellow only for CPU fallback, never red); tests added; project-context (whisper-setup, frontend-design) updated.
7. Root cause of the missed expectation is recorded in the task notes.
important_constraints:
## Root Cause Analysis (AC #7)

**What happened:** AUG-136 added the GPU engine switch exclusively to SettingsModal.tsx. The Diagnostics screen (SetupGuide.tsx) — which is the first screen users see when all components are ready — showed "Transcription runs on CPU" as a static, non-actionable text line (lines 168-171). There was no button, no link to Settings, and no indication that a switch existed.

**Why it was missed:** AUG-136 acceptance criteria specified "Settings" and "a diagnostics hint" but the hint on the Diagnostics screen had no action attached. The Diagnostics screen was treated as a status display, not as a place where users would expect to act. The user's mental model is: "I see a problem here → I fix it here." The switch was in Settings, which is a place users go to configure, not to discover capabilities.

**Root cause:** The feature was scoped to the Settings surface only. The Diagnostics screen — the primary touchpoint where the CPU limitation is surfaced — was not included in the switch flow. This is a discoverability gap: the problem is shown in one place, the solution lives in another, and nothing connects them.

**Fix:** Added a "Switch to GPU (NVIDIA)" button directly on the Diagnostics screen, inline with the CPU notice, using the same POST /api/engine/switch endpoint and SSE progress stream as the Settings switch. Handles env-var pinning gracefully with a plain-language explanation.
